primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetic nephropathy and hypertensive nephrosclerosis

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends atorvastatin 20 mg for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong — review every 3 months and titrate to target BP
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203: ACE inhibitor first‑line for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

interactions_checked.interaction: Concurrent use of two statins increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis

interactions_checked.action: No action required; monitor blood pressure and renal function as per guideline

contraindications.reason: eGFR 15.4 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 5) – NSAIDs worsen renal function and cause fluid retention (NICE NG107)
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for analgesia where appropriate

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² increases risk of lactic acidosis (NICE NG107)
Dual RAAS blockade raises risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury (NICE NG107/NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Use either an ACE‑I or an ARB alone (Ramipril chosen)

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5 predisposes to hyperkalaemia (NICE NG107)
contraindications.alternative: Restrict dietary potassium if needed; avoid supplements

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium and creatinine are required before starting Ramipril; assume values acceptable but obtain labs and repeat 1–2 weeks after initiation (NICE NG107).
Baseline liver function tests are required before switching from Simvastatin to Atorvastatin; assume normal but obtain before change (NICE NG203).
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT), haemoglobin, and erythropoietin levels are needed to consider ESA or IV iron therapy; not prescribed pending results.
Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH are needed to assess need for phosphate binders or vitamin D analogues; pending labs.
Serum bicarbonate is needed to assess metabolic acidosis before starting sodium bicarbonate; pending.
Allergy status to ACE inhibitors and statins is not documented; verify before prescribing.
treatment_summary: Start renoprotective ACE inhibition with Ramipril 2.5 mg daily and replace suboptimal Simvastatin 10 mg with guideline‑preferred Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk reduction. Monitor potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure after ACE‑I initiation, and liver function before statin switch. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy, and high‑dose potassium supplements. Additional CKD‑related therapies (ESA, IV iron, phosphate binders, vitamin D analogues, sodium bicarbonate) will be considered once relevant laboratory results are available.
